lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Velundrath archive. Lex's desk — the same one the archivists used three hundred and forty years ago. Their ink stains are still in the wood. His are joining them.

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.monologue: I open the notebook. New binding. Good paper — Suri sourced it from a mill near Verath. 'Don't ask what I paid,' she said. I didn't ask. I did calculate it based on current paper costs per ream and her expression when she handed it over. She overpaid. She'll never admit it.

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.monologue: The first line. I've been thinking about the first line for six days. The archivists who came before me — the ones who stopped writing — their last entries are all mid-sentence. One of them was cataloguing weather patterns. Another was noting the price of lamp oil. They didn't know they were writing their last words.

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.monologue: I know I'm writing my first.

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.monologue: 'In the autumn of the current age, a series of events —' No. That's a report. Reports are what people write when they don't want to be responsible for what happened.

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.monologue: I cross it out. Start again.

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.monologue: 'What follows is an account of the threshold collapse and its resolution, as witnessed by —' No. 'Witnessed.' As if I stood at a distance and took notes. I didn't stand at a distance. I was there. I was afraid. I watched Caelan step into something too large for a person and come back smaller and more real than he'd been before.

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.monologue: I cross it out. The paper is getting messy. The archivists would disapprove. I don't care about the archivists. They stopped writing. I won't.

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.monologue: 'The truth of what happened is —' The truth of what happened is bigger than sentences. That's the problem. Every word I put down is a choice to leave out ten other words. Every sentence is a frame around an experience that had no edges.

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.monologue: I sit back. I look at the crossed-out lines. I look at the ink stains of the archivists who came before me. I think about Zi, who says everything in three words or fewer. I think about Suri, who talks constantly and means something different from what she says. I think about Rynn, who talks to trees and understands them. I think about Caelan, who was once too vast for language and chose to come back to it anyway.

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.monologue: Two words. Insufficient. Imprecise. Completely true. The archivists would want more context. Dates. Names. Classifications. They'll get them. Three hundred pages of them, probably, knowing me. But the first line — the foundation the rest of it stands on — has to be the simplest true thing I can say.

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.monologue: This happened. We were there. I'm still here, and I'm writing it down, and that's the difference between this time and last time. Someone is left to hold the pen.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He fills three hundred pages after them. Every one is true. None of them are sufficient. He writes them anyway.
